title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: item (e) of a list of research directions closing the computations of §47ff. These computations concern the 'équation des lacets', the conditions on (α,β) that make an automorphism of π̂_{0,3} come from Γ_Q (Grothendieck–Teichmüller type conditions). Grothendieck's M_{0,3} is P^1 − {0,1,∞}, i.e. modern M_{0,4}. The header reads 𝔖̂^{+∧}_{0,3} → G(Ẑ)/±1, a homomorphism from the profinite 'geometric' group into the Ẑ-points of a group scheme modulo ±1.

The text says, in modern terms:
- Let 𝔐^+_{0,3} ≅ π_1([M_{0,3,Q}/S_3]) be the arithmetic orbifold fundamental group of the stack quotient of the λ-line by the anharmonic S_3-action.
- This quotient is the j-line, the rigidified stack M_{1,1}' (M_{1,1} with the generic μ_2 removed).
- So 𝔐^+_{0,3} ≅ π_1(M'_{1,1,Q}), an extension of Γ_Q by the profinite completion 𝔖̂^{+∧}_{0,3}.
- The discrete geometric group is 𝔖^+_{0,3} ≅ SL(2,Z)' (most likely PSL(2,Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3). The free group π_{0,3} ≅ Γ(2)/±1 is a normal subgroup of index 6 with quotient S_3.

Grothendieck feels he has found a systematic procedure to build 'motivic' representations of Γ_Q:
1. Start from representations ρ of the discrete group PSL(2,Z), or its variants SL(2,Z) and π_{0,3}.
2. Take ρ with values in G(Z), for G a group scheme over Z that is generically (reductive??).
3. Complete profinitely to get 𝔖̂ → G(Ẑ)/±1.
4. Use the outer Galois action on 𝔖̂ (controlled by the α,β calculus) to extend or twist, giving Γ_Q-representations into G(Ẑ). These are compatible ℓ-adic systems for all ℓ simultaneously.

He then opens item (f): another direction, not necessarily tied to group schemes, staying inside 'big' profinite fundamental groups. The next page specifies it: special rational points of P^1 − {0,1,∞} beyond the critical ones, and Ihara-type arithmetic properties.
errors: The identification π_1([M_{0,4}/S_3]) ≅ π_1(M_{1,1}) needs care. The quotient stack gives PSL(2,Z) geometrically, whereas the full stack M_{1,1} gives SL(2,Z). The prime on M_{1,1}' and on SL(2,Z)' presumably marks the μ_2-rigidified version; Grothendieck himself lists SL(2,Z) as a separate 'variant'. This is consistent but undefined on the page.

Gap: a representation of the geometric group yields a Γ_Q-representation only if its conjugacy class is stable under the outer Galois action (a rigidity condition) or if it extends to the arithmetic π_1. Nothing on the page addresses this; it is stated as a 'sentiment', not a result.
Calling such representations 'motivic' is a conjectural claim. It is not justified here, though it is now known in the rigid case (Katz).

ideas.what: Identify the S_3-orbifold quotient of P^1−{0,1,∞} with the (rigidified) moduli of elliptic curves, so that its geometric π_1 is (P)SL(2,Z) with π_{0,3} = Γ(2)/±1 of index 6.
ideas.modern_name: Legendre λ-line as X(2); [M_{0,4}/S_3] ≅ M_{1,1} rigidified
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Legendre, Klein); in Galois–Teichmüller theory Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of M_{1,1} and SL(2,Z) in the Teichmüller tower

ideas.what: Construct 'motivic' Galois representations of Γ_Q systematically. Take representations of the discrete group PSL(2,Z) (or SL(2,Z), F_2) into integral points G(Z) of reductive group schemes over Z, complete profinitely, and use the Galois action on the geometric fundamental group of M_{1,1} / P^1−{0,1,∞}.
ideas.modern_name: Galois representations from rigid / integral local systems on P^1−{0,1,∞} and M_{1,1} (Katz's rigid local systems, hypergeometric motives; Eichler–Shimura/Scholl motives from SL(2,Z)-representations); integrality of rigid local systems
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz (Rigid Local Systems, 1996); Belyi–Matzat–Thompson rigidity method; Simpson's conjecture that rigid local systems are motivic; Esnault–Groechenig (integrality, 2018); Beukers–Heckman (integral hypergeometric monodromy)
ideas.where_published: unsure; not stated in this form in the Esquisse as far as I know

ideas.what: Second programme (f): study special rational points of P^1−{0,1,∞} other than 0, 1, ∞, 1/2, 2, −1 and the sixth roots of unity, to extract arithmetic properties of π̂_{0,3} à la Ihara, and compute the Galois action on paths at these points.
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on étale path torsors / tangential and rational base points; Ihara's pro-ℓ theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Deligne (1989, tangential base points), Nakamura, Wojtkowiak

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes producing motivic representations of Γ_Q from representations of PSL(2,Z) / π_{0,3} into G(Z), with integral values and reductive target, via the Galois action on the profinite geometric π_1. This prefigures the later programme of Katz (rigid local systems on P^1 minus points are motivic, 1996), Simpson's motivicity conjecture and Esnault–Groechenig's integrality theorem. The emphasis on G(Z)-valued (integral) representations and on exploiting the explicit Galois–Teichmüller parametrisation (α,β) of the outer action is the distinctive point.
missed.quote: j'ai le sentiment d'avoir mis le doigt sur un procédé systématique pour construire les représentations "motiviques" de Γ_Q, via des représentations ... du groupe 𝔖^+_{0,3} ≃ SL(2,Z)' discret ... à valeurs dans les points entiers de schémas en groupes génériquement (réductifs ??) sur Z
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early unpublished articulation linking Galois–Teichmüller theory (the GT-type action) with integral rigid local systems and motivic Galois representations. The two literatures (GT/Ihara versus Katz/Simpson/Esnault–Groechenig) have developed largely separately. The preceding pages may contain the concrete 'systematic procedure' (calculations with SG and a 'Steinhaus homomorphism'), which deserves inspection.

missed.claim: Programme of computing the Galois action on π_{0,3} at non-critical rational points of P^1−{0,1,∞} to derive Ihara-type arithmetic properties of π̂_{0,3}. It is coupled with founding the 'équation des lacets' via a partial compactification, as suggested by Deligne.
missed.quote: Il y a pourtant une autre direction d'investigation qui m'attire beaucoup ... dans le contexte des seuls "gros" groupes fondamentaux profinis
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Partially realised later (Nakamura, Wojtkowiak, Deligne's tangential base points). Grothendieck's specific plan is only sketched, on the next page.

deep.surprise_reason: A vague but genuine anticipation of the idea that integral representations of PSL(2,Z) / F_2 together with the Galois–Teichmüller action produce motivic Galois representations. That idea later became Katz/Simpson/Esnault–Groechenig territory. It is a 'sentiment' without construction on this page, so it remains moderate.
transcription_corrections: Header and inline superscripts read '+∧' (profinite completion), not '+1': 𝔖̂^{+∧}_{0,3} → G(Ẑ)/±1. The struck letter before G looks like a cancelled P or similar.
'par nécessairement liée' should be 'pas nécessairement liée'.
'{+via+} [-des-]' should be read as 'ou mieux, via des représentations du groupe ...'.
'M^{+}_{0,3}' is probably the script 𝔐^+_{0,3} (the arithmetic group), with the S_3 in π_1(M_{0,3 Q}, 𝔖_3) denoting the orbifold quotient.
'qui pourrait se poursuivre {+dans [?]+} le contexte' should be read as 'qui pourrait se poursuivre dans le contexte des seuls "gros" groupes fondamentaux profinis'.
The insertion over 'groupes' (rendered 'invariants') is uncertain; it may be a different adjective such as 'auxiliaires'.
